q: Wind energy is the kinetic energy of air in motion. (2024)
e: Wind energy is defined as the kinetic energy associated with the movement of air masses.

q: Solar energy is indeed classified as a type of non-renewable energy. (2024)
e: Solar energy is classified as a renewable energy source.

q: Fossil fuels are renewable sources of energy. (2024)
e: Fossil fuels are non-renewable energy sources because they take millions of years to form.

q: Renewable energy sources do not pollute the environment. (2025)
e: Renewable energy sources generally produce little to no direct greenhouse gas or pollutant emissions.

q: Biomass contains stored chemical energy. (2025)
e: Biomass stores chemical energy absorbed from the sun through photosynthesis.

q: The tidal energy is produced by the difference in sea levels. (2025)
e: Tidal energy is harnessed from the rise and fall of oceanic tides causing sea-level differences.

q: At the earth's surface solar radiation has an intensity of approximately 1350 Wm^-2. (2025)
e: The solar constant of 1350 Wm^-2 is measured at the edge of the atmosphere, whereas intensity at Earth's surface is lower.

q: Due to less emission of greenhouse gases, solar energy can also improved air quality. (2025)
e: Replacing fossil fuels with solar energy reduces air pollutants and improves air quality.

q: Renewable energy sources are finite and cannot be replenished once consumed. (2025)
e: Renewable energy sources are continuously replenished naturally and are non-exhaustive.

q: Solar cell generates electricity using a chemical reaction. (2025)
e: Solar cells generate electricity via the photovoltaic effect, converting light directly into electricity.

q: Fossil fuels are replenished quickly enough to be considered a renewable energy source. (2025)
e: Fossil fuels are consumed much faster than they can form naturally.

q: Nuclear energy is a renewable energy source. (2025)
e: Nuclear energy uses finite resources like uranium and is considered non-renewable.

q: If the height of waterfall of hydroelectric power plant, is increased, the available output power will be decreased. (2025)
e: Increasing the height of the waterfall increases potential energy, which increases available output power.

q: Sun is one of the most powerful non-renewable sources of energy. (2025)
e: The Sun is a renewable source of energy.

q: The tidal energy is produced by the difference in sea levels. (2025)
e: Tidal power utilizes the vertical water height difference created by tides.

q: Solar energy is a type of non-renewable energy. (2025)
e: Solar energy is an abundant renewable energy source.

q: A solar cell is basically a p-n junction diode. (2025)
e: Photovoltaic solar cells are semiconductor p-n junction devices designed to absorb photons and generate electric current.

q: Flat plate collectors are the least common type of collector. (2026)
e: Flat plate collectors are actually the most common type of solar collector used for water heating.

q: The sun emits the maximum irradiance in the infrared region of the spectrum. (2026)
e: According to textbook context provided, this statement is marked as true.

q: Solar collectors transfer heat from solar radiation to water. (2026)
e: Solar thermal collectors capture solar radiation energy and transfer it to a working fluid such as water.
